data.name: Everolimus
data.description: Rapamycin analog (RAD001); used in oncology and tested for immune function in older adults.
data.description_beginner: A modified version of rapamycin. Used in cancer treatment and also studied for boosting immune responses in older adults.

reading_levels.beginner: A rapamycin derivative used in clinic.
reading_levels.student: Rapalog licensed in several cancers and in tuberous sclerosis complex.
reading_levels.research: RAD001. Same FKBP12-dependent allosteric mechanism as rapamycin, better oral pharmacokinetics; the clinical evidence base here is trial evidence, not mechanism.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition improves immune function in the elderly
studies.authors: Mannick JB; Del Giudice G; Lattanzi M; Valiante NM; Praestgaard J; Huang B; Lonetto MA; Maecker HT; Kovarik J; Carson S; Glass DJ; Klickstein LB

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Older volunteers took the rapalog everolimus (RAD001) before a flu shot, and their antibody response to the vaccine rose by about 20% at doses that were fairly well tolerated. The share of T cells carrying the exhaustion marker PD-1 also fell. The PEARL authors summarise the doses as 0.5 mg daily or 5 mg weekly for 6 weeks. This is the human result behind the weekly low-dose idea. Boundary: a stronger vaccine response is a lab marker, not fewer infections, and the later RTB101 trial (MAN2021) shows how that gap can matter.

studies.title: Efficacy of everolimus in advanced renal cell carcinoma: a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled phase III trial
studies.authors: Motzer RJ; Escudier B; Oudard S; Hutson TE; Porta C; Bracarda S; Grünwald V; Thompson JA; Figlin RA; Hollaender N; Urbanowitz G; Berg WJ; Kay A; Lebwohl D; Ravaud A

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Everolimus extended median progression-free survival from 1.9 to 4.0 months versus placebo in metastatic renal cell carcinoma.

studies.title: Everolimus for subependymal giant-cell astrocytomas in tuberous sclerosis
studies.authors: Krueger DA; Care MM; Holland K; Agricola K; Tudor C; Mangeshkar P; Wilson KA; Byars A; Sahmoud T; Franz DN

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In patients whose TSC1/TSC2 mutations cause brain tumors, everolimus shrank tumor volume by 30%+ in three-quarters of patients. Open-label and uncontrolled (n=28); randomised confirmation came later (FRA2013).

studies.title: Everolimus Aging Study (EVERLAST): Clinical Evaluation of mTORC1 Inhibition for Geroprotection
studies.authors: University of Wisconsin, Madison (registered trial)

evidence.label: Registered trial, no results yet
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Phase 2 trial (NCT05835999, EVERLAST) testing this Atlas's open dosing hypothesis directly: whether daily low-dose (0.5 mg/day) or weekly (5 mg/week) everolimus for 24 weeks can improve physiological and molecular hallmarks of aging in insulin-resistant or prediabetic adults aged 55-80, without the metabolic penalty seen with continuous higher-dose rapalog use. Double-blind and placebo-controlled with four arms (everolimus daily, everolimus weekly, and a matching placebo for each), n=106, plus a separate untreated 18-35 cohort for comparison. Primary endpoint is peripheral insulin sensitivity by dual-tracer OGTT; mTORC1 and mTORC2 signalling are secondary endpoints in muscle and blood cells. STATUS: the registry records the trial as COMPLETED, with primary completion 2026-06-30 and completion 2026-07-22. No results are posted yet, so there is nothing to read into the outcome either way.

studies.title: Targeting ageing with rapamycin and its derivatives in humans: a systematic review
studies.authors: Lee DJW; Hodzic Kuerec A; Maier AB

evidence.label: Synthesis of human data
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Described by its authors as the first systematic review of rapamycin/rapalogs in humans for aging. Screened 18,400 articles, included 19 studies. Found improvements in immune, cardiovascular, and skin (integumentary) parameters; NO significant effect on endocrine, muscular, or neurological systems. No serious adverse events in healthy people, but more infections and raised cholesterol/triglycerides in people with age-related disease. This is the highest-tier human-evidence summary in the whole Atlas - it aggregates many individual human studies rather than reporting one.

studies.title: TORC1 inhibition enhances immune function and reduces infections in the elderly
studies.authors: Mannick JB; Morris M; Hockey HP; Roma G; Beibel M; Kulmatycki K; Watkins M; Shavlakadze T; Zhou W; Quinn D; Glass DJ; Klickstein LB

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: A phase 2a RCT in 264 older adults: 6 weeks of a low-dose combination of BEZ235 (a catalytic PI3K/mTOR inhibitor) and everolimus (RAD001) was associated with fewer reported infections over the following year, plus higher antiviral gene expression and a better flu-vaccine response. The later phase 3 trial of RTB101 (BEZ235) alone (MAN2021) did not confirm a clinical benefit.

studies.title: Everolimus in postmenopausal hormone-receptor-positive advanced breast cancer (BOLERO-2)
studies.authors: Baselga J; Campone M; Piccart M; Burris HA; Rugo HS; Sahmoud T; Noguchi S; Gnant M; Pritchard KI; Lebrun F; Beck JT; Ito Y; Yardley D; Deleu I; Perez A; Bachelot T; Vittori L; Xu Z; Mukhopadhyay P; Lebwohl D; Hortobagyi GN

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: A phase 3 RCT (n=724) proving mTOR matters in a common cancer. Resistance to hormone therapy in breast cancer is associated with mTOR activation. Adding everolimus more than doubled progression-free survival (10.6 vs 4.1 months by central review) - leading to FDA approval. Main toxicity was stomatitis.

studies.title: Everolimus for advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (RADIANT-3)
studies.authors: Yao JC; Shah MH; Ito T; Bohas CL; Wolin EM; Van Cutsem E; Hobday TJ; Okusaka T; Capdevila J; de Vries EG; Tomassetti P; Pavel ME; Hoosen S; Haas T; Lincy J; Lebwohl D; Oberg K

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: A phase 3 RCT (n=410) that made everolimus a standard treatment for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. It more than doubled progression-free survival (11.0 vs 4.6 months, a 65% reduction in risk of progression/death) with mostly mild side effects. Another FDA-approved indication built on blocking mTOR.

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of everolimus for subependymal giant cell astrocytomas associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (EXIST-1): a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial
studies.authors: Franz DN; Belousova E; Sparagana S; Bebin EM; Frost M; Kuperman R; Witt O; Kohrman MH; Flamini JR; Wu JY; Curatolo P; de Vries PJ; Whittemore VH; Thiele EA; Ford JP; Shah G; Cauwel H; Lebwohl D; Sahmoud T; Jozwiak S

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Phase 3 RCT (n=117) in tuberous sclerosis, the disease where mTOR is stuck ON by a genetic fault. Everolimus shrank brain tumors (SEGA) by >=50% in 35% of patients versus 0% on placebo. Because the underlying cause here is direct mTOR overactivation, this is arguably the cleanest randomised human evidence that blocking mTOR works in a genetically defined mTORopathy -- which does not extend to mTOR inhibition in people without such a mutation.

studies.title: Everolimus for angiomyolipoma associated with tuberous sclerosis complex or sporadic lymphangioleiomyomatosis (EXIST-2): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
studies.authors: Bissler JJ; Kingswood JC; Radzikowska E; Zonnenberg BA; Frost M; Belousova E; Sauter M; Nonomura N; Brakemeier S; de Vries PJ; Whittemore VH; Chen D; Sahmoud T; Shah G; Lincy J; Lebwohl D; Budde K

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The companion phase 3 RCT (n=118) to EXIST-1, targeting kidney tumors (angiomyolipomas) in tuberous sclerosis and LAM. Everolimus shrank them by >=50% in 42% of patients versus 0% on placebo. Together EXIST-1 and -2 sealed everolimus as a disease-modifying therapy across multiple TSC tumor types.

studies.title: EVERolimus effectiveness after proGREssion on ENdocrine therapy plus CDK4/6 inhibitor for ER-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer: EVERGREEN study
studies.authors: Diogo Martins-Branco, Soraia Lobo-Martins, Philippe Aftimos, Bernardo Pereira, Leonor Vasconcelos de Matos, Leonor Fernandes, Guilherme Nader-Marta, Michel Moreau, Donatienne Taylor, Francois P Duhoux, Evandro de Azambuja

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Everolimus added to endocrine therapy provided modest but statistically significant PFS benefit (5.0 vs 4.3 months; HR 0.68) in ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer post-CDK4/6 inhibitor progression, without demonstrable OS benefit, supporting selective use. Retrospective and non-randomised, so treatment-selection bias cannot be excluded.

studies.title: Everolimus for the treatment of neuropsychological deficits in tuberous sclerosis complex: findings from the TRON multicentre randomised controlled trial
studies.authors: Saxena A; Drew CJ; Cannings-John R; Pickles T; Mills LJ; McDermott E; Angel L; McNamara R; Smalley M; Randell E; Joss SK; Donnelly DE; Davies DM; Owen-Jones E; Kirby N; de Vries PJ; Hood K; Sampson JR

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In a multicentre RCT of TSC patients (n=38 randomised, 2:1 everolimus:placebo), 24 weeks of everolimus produced similarly large 'responder' rates for neuropsychological improvement as placebo (87% vs 75%), suggesting large practice/placebo effects rather than a clear drug benefit on cognition -- despite everolimus's established efficacy for TSC tumours and epilepsy. Adverse events were more frequent with everolimus (88% vs 61.5%).

studies.title: Tumor fat composition predicts response to everolimus and supports low-dose therapy in TSC-associated renal angiomyolipomas: a multicenter prospective study
studies.authors: Gao K; Duan Y; Ren B; Guo B; Su R; Gu H; Chen F; Zhang C; Wu G; Ni J

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human (TSC-associated renal angiomyolipoma patients, multicenter prospective cohort, n=183)
studies.finding: In a multicenter prospective cohort of 183 TSC-associated renal angiomyolipoma patients, everolimus reduced tumor volume by >=50% in 44% of patients at 3 months and 83% at 6 months; fat-poor lesions responded significantly better than fat-rich ones. No significant difference in response was detected between the low-dose and standard-dose groups in an exploratory, non-randomised subset, and oral mucositis was less frequent on the low dose; tumor regrowth occurred after treatment discontinuation.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition augments antitumor immune effector response by reprogramming the TP53-mutant, immune-cold HNSCC tumor microenvironment
studies.authors: Nath P; Khandelwal A; Li C; Moore-Medlin T; Vasudevan SS; Alvarez VA; Franco OE; Gutkind JS; Nathan CO

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Syngeneic mouse models of TP53-mutant HNSCC
studies.finding: In syngeneic TP53-mutant HNSCC mouse models, the mTOR inhibitor everolimus reprogrammed the immune-cold tumor microenvironment: it increased CD8+ T cell and dendritic cell infiltration, reduced Tregs and HIF-1α/VEGFA-driven MDSC recruitment, boosted TNF-α/CXCL10 chemokine signaling, and reduced PD-1/PD-L1 expression — restoring T-cell cytotoxic competence and suppressing tumor growth.

studies.title: Circadian regulation of mTOR by the ubiquitin pathway in renal cell carcinoma
studies.authors: Okazaki H; Matsunaga N; Fujioka T; Okazaki F; Akagawa Y; Tsurudome Y; Ono M; Kuwano M; Koyanagi S; Ohdo S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In mouse kidney tumours, active phosphorylated mTOR and total mTOR protein followed a 24-hour rhythm, set by the clock through the ubiquitin ligase Fbxw7. Giving everolimus when mTOR was high improved survival compared with other dosing times. Same drug, same dose - the clock time of dosing changed the outcome.

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of everolimus in heart transplant recipients: A meta-analysis
studies.authors: Vitte SH; Luna AM; Pille JJ; Pinheiro BN; Souza MBL; Irudhayaraj CDJ; Munaretto GM

evidence.label: Synthesis of human data
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human (adult and paediatric heart transplant recipients)
studies.finding: Meta-analysis of 60 studies (1786 heart transplant recipients): everolimus-based immunosuppression reduced cardiac allograft vasculopathy progression on IVUS (RR ~0.57) and preserved renal function (eGFR +10-15 mL/min) when combined with calcineurin-inhibitor minimisation, with neutral all-cause mortality (RR ~0.98) but more adverse events and treatment discontinuation.

studies.title: [177Lu]Lu-edotreotide versus everolimus for gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (COMPETE): a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, open-label, superiority trial.
studies.authors: Walter T; Jann H; Ansquer C; Deshayes E; Garcia-Carbonero R; Teulé A; Baum RP; Verberne HJ; Ćwikła JB; Srirajaskanthan R; de Mestier L; Grana CM; Buck A; Hörsch D; Pavel M; Dierickx LO; Michael M; Strosberg J; Kollár A; Jimenez-Fonseca P; Rinke A; Del Olmo-García M; Flaus A; Hernando J; Kluge A; Breuninger M; Melnyk S; Zhernosekov K; Capdevila J

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Phase 3 open-label RCT (n=309, 2:1): 177Lu-edotreotide gave longer PFS than everolimus (23.9 vs 14.1 months; HR 0.67) with fewer grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events (18% vs 40%), supporting PRRT in early lines for progressive SSTR-positive GEP-NETs.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition induces upstream receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and activates Akt
studies.authors: O'Reilly KE; Rojo F; She QB; Solit D; Mills GB; Smith D; Lane H; Hofmann F; Hicklin DJ; Ludwig DL; Baselga J; Rosen N

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Cancer cell lines + patient tumours treated with the rapamycin derivative RAD001 (everolimus)
studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibition relieves feedback and activates upstream RTK-PI3K-Akt signalling. The Akt activation was demonstrated both in cancer cell lines and in patient tumours treated with RAD001 (everolimus), so this record carries a human pharmacodynamic component, not only in-vitro data.

studies.title: Response of a neuronal model of tuberous sclerosis to mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors: effects on mTORC1 and Akt signaling lead to improved survival and function
studies.authors: Meikle L; Pollizzi K; Egnor A; Kramvis I; Lane H; Sahin M; Kwiatkowski DJ

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: mTOR inhibition rescues a neuronal tuberous-sclerosis model, supporting rapamycin for TSC neurology.

studies.title: Does the duration of exposure to everolimus influence the occurrence of chronic lung allograft dysfunction?
studies.authors: Landoas A; Perrier Q; Falque L; Saint-Raymond C; Briault A; Degano B; Chanoine S; Bedouch P

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In lung transplant recipients, later introduction of everolimus and a greater number of treatment interruptions were both risk factors for chronic lung allograft dysfunction; earlier, uninterrupted treatment was associated with lower CLAD risk (retrospective, single-centre; causality not established).

studies.title: SPOP-mediated ZMYND8 ubiquitination and phase separation exclusion drives mTOR inhibitor resistance in kidney cancer
studies.authors: Tang B; Sun R; Shao J; Wu QY; Yan Y; Wang D; Yu Z; Hu L; Chen Y; Liao C; Wei Q; Bao Y; Huang H

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: ccRCC cell lines (in vitro); mouse xenograft tumors treated with a NEK7-targeting PROTAC
studies.finding: Identifies a mechanism of mTOR-inhibitor (everolimus/temsirolimus) resistance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma: SPOP-driven K63-linked ubiquitination of ZMYND8 excludes it from phase-separation compartments, enabling a ZMYND8-ZHX2 complex that drives NEK7 transcription and alternative p70S6K activation independent of mTOR inhibition. A NEK7-targeting PROTAC restored everolimus sensitivity in ccRCC cells and mouse tumors, nominating NEK7 as a target to overcome mTOR-inhibitor resistance.

studies.title: Everolimus plus exemestane for hormone-receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor-2-negative advanced breast cancer: overall survival results from BOLERO-2†
studies.authors: Piccart M; Hortobagyi GN; Campone M; Pritchard KI; Lebrun F; Ito Y; Noguchi S; Perez A; Rugo HS; Deleu I; Burris HA; Provencher L; Neven P; Gnant M; Shtivelband M; Wu C; Fan J; Feng W; Taran T; Baselga J

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Humans: postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer after nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitors; phase III RCT, everolimus + exemestane vs placebo + exemestane (2:1)
studies.finding: This is the final overall-survival report of BOLERO-2, the phase III double-blind trial (published primary analysis: BAS2012) in which postmenopausal women with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer that had progressed on a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor received exemestane 25 mg/day plus either everolimus 10 mg/day or placebo. The primary endpoint, progression-free survival by local investigator, remained improved: median 7.8 vs 3.2 months (P < 0.0001), a 4.6-month gain. Overall survival, a key secondary endpoint, was not significantly improved: median 31.0 vs 26.6 months, hazard ratio 0.89 (95% CI 0.73-1.10), P = 0.14, at 410 deaths. Most patients went on to further treatment after the trial (84% vs 90%), with less chemotherapy in the everolimus arm (53% vs 63%), which may have diluted any survival difference. No new safety concerns were identified. Boundary: postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer previously treated with a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor; comparator was exemestane plus placebo; the survival benefit of adding mTOR inhibition was not shown.

studies.title: Adjunctive everolimus therapy for treatment-resistant focal-onset seizures associated with tuberous sclerosis (EXIST-3): a phase 3, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
studies.authors: French JA; Lawson JA; Yapici Z; Ikeda H; Polster T; Nabbout R; Curatolo P; de Vries PJ; Dlugos DJ; Berkowitz N; Voi M; Peyrard S; Pelov D; Franz DN

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Humans: 366 patients aged 2-65 with TSC and treatment-resistant focal-onset seizures on 1-3 antiepileptic drugs; phase 3 RCT, placebo vs low-exposure (trough 3-7 ng/mL) vs high-exposure (9-15 ng/mL) everolimus; 99 centres, 25 countries
studies.finding: EXIST-3 was a phase 3, double-blind trial in 366 patients aged 2 to 65 with tuberous sclerosis complex and focal seizures that had not responded to standard drugs. They were randomised 1:1:1 to placebo (n=119), everolimus dosed to a low blood trough of 3-7 ng/mL (n=117) or a high trough of 9-15 ng/mL (n=130), added to their existing antiepileptic drugs. For the primary endpoint, at least a 50% fall in seizure frequency during the 12-week maintenance period, the response rate was 15.1% with placebo, 28.2% with low exposure (p=0.0077) and 40.0% with high exposure (p<0.0001); median seizure reduction was 14.9%, 29.3% and 39.6%. Grade 3-4 adverse events occurred in 11%, 18% and 24%, and serious adverse events in 3%, 14% and 14% of patients, respectively. The result showed a dose-dependent effect of mTOR inhibition on seizures in TSC, beyond its known effect on TSC tumours. Boundary: patients with TSC and treatment-resistant focal-onset seizures already on 1-3 antiepileptic drugs; comparator was placebo add-on; 18-week core phase (6-week titration, 12-week maintenance), so long-term durability is not addressed here.

relations.mechanism: BOLERO-2: adding everolimus to hormone therapy roughly doubled progression-free survival in hormone-receptor-positive advanced breast cancer.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Adding everolimus to hormone therapy roughly doubled the time before certain advanced breast cancers got worse.
relations.boundary: Progression-free survival, in combination with exemestane - overall survival was not significantly improved.
relations.note: Say PFS, not survival. The distinction is the whole argument of this Atlas.

relations.mechanism: Dose and schedule set the direction here, not the target. Intermittent low-dose everolimus improved influenza vaccine responses in older adults (MAN2014), while continuous transplant-level dosing of the same drug class is immunosuppressive. A larger phase 3 trial of a different mTOR inhibitor, RTB101 (an ATP-competitive PI3K/mTOR inhibitor), did not reduce respiratory illness (MAN2021), although it still switched on antiviral genes. The edge carries a conditional sign because the supported claim is regimen-specific rather than a net benefit to immune function.
relations.mechanism_beginner: At a low, occasional dose, an mTOR-blocking drug helped older people respond better to a flu vaccine. At the high continuous dose used after transplants, mTOR inhibitors damp the immune system down. A larger phase 3 trial of a DIFFERENT mTOR inhibitor (RTB101, which blocks the kinase itself rather than working like rapamycin) found no reduction in respiratory illness – so what this arrow means depends on the dose, the schedule and the drug.
relations.context: Direction depends on dose and schedule. Transplant-level dosing is immunosuppressive; intermittent low dosing improved vaccine responses in older adults. Treating this as one effect with one sign is the error.
relations.boundary: Dose-dependent and duration-dependent: this is not the immunosuppressive regimen. The corpus supports an improved vaccine response under one regimen, not improved immune function in general. MAN2021 is recorded as conflicting for two reasons, and the earlier wording here got the first one wrong. Its phase 3 arm tested RTB101 monotherapy - a different drug, ATP-competitive rather than rapamycin-like - and found no reduction in clinically symptomatic respiratory illness. But the same paper's phase 2b part 2 DID include everolimus: 115 participants were randomised to RTB101 10 mg plus everolimus 0.1 mg daily, and that arm did not reach significance in the first prespecified analysis of the primary endpoint. So the randomised everolimus-containing evidence in MAN2021 points away from benefit as well, at a different dose and in a different population from MAN2014, rather than being irrelevant to this edge. Note also that the positive RTB101 10 mg result in that paper comes from a second prespecified analysis pooling parts 1 and 2, not from the first.
relations.note: THE dose-dependence case study, and a genuine apparent contradiction with the drug's immunosuppressant label. Prime Contradiction Engine seed.

relations.mechanism: EXIST-2 tested everolimus against renal angiomyolipoma in patients with tuberous sclerosis or sporadic LAM, and shrank those lesions by >=50% in 42% versus 0% on placebo.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In another trial, everolimus shrank kidney growths in patients with tuberous sclerosis or a related lung disease, working in 42% of patients versus 0% on placebo.
relations.boundary: Scope: the endpoint was the kidney lesion, not LAM lung disease, which is why this arrow lands on the angiomyolipoma and not on LAM. The evidence that mTOR inhibition treats the lung disease itself is the MILES trial with sirolimus - see the RAPA-LAM edge.
relations.note: Rescoped 2026-07-29: this edge previously read as though everolimus had been shown to treat LAM.

relations.mechanism: Everolimus is rapamycin with a solubilising side chain - same FKBP12 mechanism, better oral pharmacokinetics. It is the molecule that carried this pathway into routine clinical use.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Everolimus is rapamycin with a small chemical tweak that makes it easier to take as a pill – same mechanism, better drug.
relations.boundary: Clinical evidence from phase 3 trials of everolimus in specific diseases (kidney cancer, breast cancer, pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours, TSC and LAM) at the doses used for those diseases. It does not speak to low-dose use in healthy ageing.
relations.note: Six trials behind one arrow. They establish the clinical effect of the drug; the allosteric mechanism itself rests on the rapamycin biochemistry.

relations.mechanism: RADIANT-3: progression-free survival more than doubled in advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In a trial, everolimus more than doubled the time before advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours got worse.
relations.boundary: One phase 3 trial (RADIANT-3, n=410) in advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours. The result applies to that disease, stage and dose, and it is a progression-free survival result.

relations.mechanism: RECORD-1: everolimus roughly doubled progression-free survival after other targeted therapy failed.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In a clinical trial, everolimus roughly doubled the time before advanced kidney cancer got worse, after other treatments had stopped working.
relations.boundary: Second-line setting, after VEGF-targeted therapy - not first-line.

relations.mechanism: EXIST trials: everolimus shrank the brain tumours (SEGA) and kidney lesions of tuberous sclerosis - treating the pathway the mutation switches on, rather than a downstream symptom. The gene defect itself remains.
relations.mechanism_beginner: In patients with the genetic disease tuberous sclerosis, everolimus shrank both brain and kidney tumours. It works one step downstream of the mutation: it replaces the brake the mutation removed, so the tumours shrink while the drug is given and regrow when it stops. The mutation itself is untouched.
relations.boundary: Lesions regrow when the drug is stopped - this is suppression, not cure.
relations.note: The purest case in the Atlas: known gene, known pathway, matched drug, randomised evidence.
